description: Rust progressive 1080p 420: 30899 µs. C libjpeg-turbo: 30358 µs. Delta: +541 µs (+1.8%). Baseline (non-prog): Rust 11109 µs, C 11376 µs. Progressive overhead: 19790 µs (2.78x). Profiled hotspots: Huffman table resolution inside inner loops, is_multiple_of modulo per MCU, no fast AC combined path in progressive AC first, per-block unwrap() calls.

Hoist table resolution + countdown restart + fast AC combined path + unsafe ZIGZAG + split non-interleaved loops. 1080p 420: 30899→29611 µs (-4.2%). Now 2.5% faster than C (29611 vs 30358). All 5 progressive sizes beat C by 2-3%. Baseline unaffected.

Branchless apply_correction_bit using arithmetic shift for sign. 1080p 420: 29611→30058 µs (+1.5% regression). Branch predictor handles the sign check efficiently since most coefficients are positive in practice. Reverted.

Batch correction bit reads in EOB path using peek_bits(16) + manual bit extraction. 1080p 420: neutral (+0 µs). 64-bit bit buffer already makes individual read_bits(1) fast. Reverted for simpler code.
Enable fast AC combined path for all al values (not just al=0). Also deduplicate Huffman decode paths in decode_ac_first — merged fast+slow paths. Code simplification with neutral performance.

P4-136 criterion 3: measured zero-init vs the uninit set_len pattern on ProgressiveDecoder, 8K progressive fixture, best-of-7, two independent pairs. Uninit: 52.27 / 52.32 ms. Zero-init (vec![0u8; size]): 54.89 / 54.69 ms. Zero-init costs ~2.5 ms (+4.7%), reproducible, not noise -- which FALSIFIES the issue hypothesis that calloc-backed pages make it free. Kept anyway: ProgressiveDecoder is an opt-in public API (src/lib.rs:210) that no benchmark and no main decode path exercises, so 4.7% on a cold path is a bad trade for a documented UB pattern. If it ever becomes hot, MaybeUninit with a written invariant is the sanctioned route and this number is the justification. Harness: examples/p4136_prog_bench.rs.

P4-136 criterion 4: replaced vec![0u8; size] (alloc_zeroed/calloc) with try_reserve_exact + resize so allocator refusal returns JpegError::AllocationFailed instead of aborting. Same 8K progressive fixture and harness (examples/p4136_prog_bench.rs), best-of-7, two independent pairs, run back-to-back on one host. main (calloc): 52.30 / 52.05 ms. This change (malloc+memset): 52.24 / 52.23 ms. Neutral -- the delta is inside each pair own spread, so trading calloc lazy zero pages for an explicit memset costs nothing at this size. ALSO: the 54.89 / 54.69 ms zero-init figure in the row above did NOT reproduce -- main today measures 52.05-52.30, i.e. at that row own *uninit* number. Treat the recorded +4.7% zero-init cost as unconfirmed; on this host zero-init is free, which is what the issue hypothesis predicted.
